question.text: Under Section 15-I of the SEBI Act, what process must the Adjudicating Officer follow before imposing any penalty?

answer.text: Hold an inquiry after giving the person a reasonable opportunity of being heard and record findings in writing
Simply issue a penalty notice based on the investigation report
Obtain prior approval from the SAT before imposing the penalty
Refer the matter to criminal court for determination of penalty

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 15-I of the SEBI Act, the Adjudicating Officer (AO) must hold an inquiry into the alleged contravention, give the person concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard, and record the findings in writing before imposing any penalty. This three-step process — inquiry, hearing, written findings — embeds the principles of natural justice into the AO's quasi-judicial penalty function. The Trap: Simply issuing a penalty notice on the investigation report bypasses the inquiry and hearing requirement. SAT approval is not required at the imposition stage — SAT is the appellate forum. Referring the matter to a criminal court mis-classifies an administrative penalty as a criminal prosecution. Note: The specific Section 15-I requirements (inquiry, reasonable opportunity of being heard, findings recorded in writing) are not stated in the cited NISM Series III-C Securities Intermediaries Compliance (Fund) workbook pages checked. The framing above is presented as general statutory / SEBI Act knowledge rather than as a workbook citation.
